title: AWS Organizations, SCPs & Control Tower
summary: Multi-account governance: guardrails with SCPs and RCPs, landing zones with Control Tower.
tldr: **SCPs** cap what principals in member accounts can do; **RCPs** cap what anyone (even outside the org) can do to resources in member accounts. Neither ever grants a permission.
**Declarative policies** enforce service settings (IMDSv2 defaults, block public AMIs/snapshots) that account admins can't change.
**Control Tower** builds a landing zone in days: log archive and audit accounts, preventive/detective/proactive controls, and **Account Factory** for new accounts.
Run security services from a **delegated administrator** account, not the management account.

keyFacts.text: SCPs and RCPs **never** apply to the management account. Keep workloads out of it, because a Region-deny SCP won't stop anyone there.
If `FullAWSAccess` is replaced at an OU, only actions the OU's SCP allows remain available. Add the service to the allow-list to unblock it.
`aws:PrincipalOrgID` in a bucket, ECR or KMS policy admits every current and future account in the org; `aws:PrincipalOrgPaths` narrows it to an OU.
SCPs and RCPs don't restrict service-linked roles, and RCPs don't apply to AWS managed KMS keys.
Control Tower controls are **preventive** (SCP/RCP), **detective** (AWS Config rules) and **proactive** (CloudFormation hooks that block noncompliant resources before creation).

traps: An SCP that allows an action does not grant it; the account still needs an IAM policy that allows it.
Instances launched from the **management account** escape every SCP, so a Region-deny there is useless.
An SCP can't stop someone outside your org from using an over-permissive bucket policy; that is what an RCP is for.
Detective controls (Config rules) only report after creation; to block creation pick preventive or **proactive** controls.
